claims.text: Adding 2–4 at% B to a phosphorus-containing FeCrMnCoNi-based high-entropy alloy will improve its glass-forming ability.
Adding 2–4 at% B will improve the thermal stability of the alloy's amorphous state.
B addition increases local network connectivity.
Increased local network connectivity suppresses crystalline nucleation.
A melt-spun FeCrMnCoNi-based alloy containing approximately 5 at% P can exhibit an amorphous or near-amorphous structure.
B forms local B–P and B–metal interactions in the proposed alloy.
B–P and B–metal interactions enhance local bonding and network connectivity.
Enhanced network connectivity produces a more homogeneous amorphous structure with fewer nucleation sites.
B doping stabilizes chemically short-range-ordered clusters.
Stabilization of chemically short-range-ordered clusters disrupts the formation of incipient crystalline nuclei.
B doping increases the activation-energy barrier for crystallization.
An increased crystallization barrier enhances the stability of the amorphous state.
B-doped samples will have a wider supercooled-liquid region than an undoped sample processed under identical conditions.
B-doped samples will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature than the undoped baseline.
A wider supercooled-liquid region and higher crystallization-onset temperature indicate improved glass-forming ability and amorphous-state thermal stability.
The beneficial effect is restricted to an optimal B concentration within 2–4 at%.
B concentrations above the optimal range could cause phase separation or secondary-phase formation.
Phase separation or secondary-phase formation would negate the proposed stabilization effect.
The proposed improvement is expected under melt-spinning cooling conditions and may not occur at slower cooling rates.
